newsitem.title: UK: MARITIME PIRACY TO INCREASE UNLESS ACTION TAKEN.
newsitem.headline: MARITIME PIRACY TO INCREASE UNLESS ACTION TAKEN.

text.p: The menace of maritime piracy will continue to increase unless co-ordinated action is taken to stop it, the leading international agency monitoring maritime crime said on Thursday.

At least seven crew members have been killed and 19 injured in piracy and armed robbery attacks on shipping around the world in the first six months of this year, said the London-based International Maritime Bureau (IMB), an arm of the International Chamber of Commerce.
"Piracy flourishes and unless positive action is taken, we are on course for an increase in incidents," said Eric Ellen, IMB executive director in the forward to a new report on maritime piracy.
However, the IMB said there were no simple solutions to cutting down the number of pirate attacks.
While initiatives are being made to police the seas more effectively, there remains a lack of a co-ordinated response on-shore to punish offenders.
The number of organised acts of piracy has risen from 64 in 1990 to 224 in 1996, according to IMB figures.
The highest numbers of pirate attacks occur in waters around Southeast Asia, and off Somalia and Brazil.
